retrieved.content: We extract a large-scale stance detection dataset from comments written by candidates of elections in Switzerland. The dataset consists of German, French and Italian text, allowing for a cross-lingual evaluation of stance detection. It contains 67 000 comments on more than 150 political issues (targets). Unlike stance detection models that have specific target issues, we use the dataset to train a single model on all the issues. To make learning across targets possible, we prepend to each instance a natural question that represents the target (e.g."Do you support X?"). Baseline results from multilingual BERT show that zero-shot cross-lingual and cross-target transfer of stance detection is moderately successful with this approach.

retrieved.content: First of all, it is questionable how well current stance detection methods perform in a cross-lingual setting, as the multilingual datasets available today are relatively small, and specific to a single target BIBREF2, BIBREF3. Furthermore, specific models tend to be developed for each single target or pair of targets BIBREF4. Concerns have been raised that cross-target performance is often considerably lower than fully supervised performance BIBREF1.
